newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank says tight liquidity to remain.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank says tight liquidity to remain.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Thursday it had not injected funds to ease liquidity in the local market as such funds could be used by banks to speculate on the rising U.S. dollar.

"If the Bank of Thailand (BoT) injected funds during this period, there will be use of such funds to speculate in the foreign exchagne market due to the dollar's upward trend," the central governor Rerngchai Marakanond told reporters.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted at around 14.50 percent at midday compared with 13.75-14.00 in early trade, dealers said.
"If the BOT wants the interbank rate to be lower, we can do so. But the current interbank rate of 13-14 percent is an appropriate level," Rerngchai said.
Tight money supply was also due to outflow of funds after recent sales of Thai stocks by foreign investors, he added.
